To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the excitation spectra for the isotropic triangular antiferromagnet show several anomalies that differ strongly from those predicted by linear spin-wave theory and that these anomalies are consistent with a description in terms of itinerant spinons.

the excitation spectra on anisotropic frustrated triangular lattices show several anomalous properties that differ strongly from LSWT, and that these properties can be explained naturally in terms of spinon physics.

the excitation spectra in frustrated quantum antifer-magnets are strongly renormalized and that the deviations from linear spin-wave-theory become more and more pronounced with increasing frustration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the magnetic properties of low-dimensional quantum antiferromagnetic systems.
quantum spin systems in which the ground state has a nonmagnetic, noncollinear order.
the study of frustrated quantum antiferrmagnets on an anisotropic triangular lattice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anomalous excitation spectra are a consequence of strong quantum effects in frustrated quantum antifer­magnets.
the spin-1/ 2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet on a triangular lattice has a Néel ground state and an excitation spectrum which deviates strongly from LSWT.
the spin-1/ 2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet on anisotropic lattices is an extremely interesting and challenging model system, which has not yet been completely understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quantum fluctuations in frustrated quantum antifer-magnets lead to a variety of exotic phenomena.
the spinon description of frustrated quantum antiferrmagnets is not only a useful theoretical tool, but also a realistic description of the low-lying spin excitations.
quantum fluctuations are much more important in frustrated quantum antifer-romagnets than in conventional ones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even at low temperatures, the excitation spectra in frustrated antiferromagnetics are very far from the predictions of LSWT.
LSWT is not a good starting point for the analysis of frustrated quantum antifers, even at zero temperature, and that spinon-based approaches should be used instead.
the excitation spectra in frustrated quantum antifer-magnets are very sensitive to quantum fluctuations, which should be taken into account when interpreting experiments.
